name: Hana Abbott

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What happens on an ordinary shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Hana, 43, and I lead five people on the yoghurt-pot filling line at a dairy plant. My two-year technical diploma covered filling controls, but the trick is hearing a sealer start to drag before twenty trays have wrinkled lids. I like solving that little sound; washing fruit pulp out of a jammed filler at night is less lovely.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How do the job and household bills fit together?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Jonas teaches at a school, and we have two children there ourselves and a mortgage. I earn about the normal rate for a line lead, have four months of expenses saved, and there are some other food plants nearby. I use AI every day to search fault logs and draft handover notes, but I check every setting at the machine.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew an AI handover note can save ten minutes, but a wrinkled lid still needs someone to stop the sealer. I would ask the office to put those ten minutes back into cleaning time rather than a faster target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our two wages cover the mortgage, and four months saved gives us a little room if a shift changes. This small software gain would leave my line-lead work and pay sound, though I still count the children's lunch bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep setting the filler and checking the first sealed pots after each fruit changeover. I would keep using my existing AI log search, then put a new amount from each full paid month into the repair fund after our regular bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm, mostly. I would rather have a clean seal than another clever report, but I am not scared for my wage here.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which fault makes you stop the line?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last Tuesday a lid looked smooth until I tipped the pot and found yoghurt on the seam. I stopped the filler and had the next tray checked before anything went to packing. A neat shift report cannot seal a leaking yoghurt pot.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What is the repair fund for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our washing machine is making a grinding noise, and four months of savings is for a real income gap as well as repairs. I would add money from new wages while the full shifts last; I would not call moving old savings into another account a gain.

say: I would tell colleagues **sealed pots** still need physical checks after a modest AI shortcut.
I would ask management to use **saved minutes** for proper cleaning, rather than a faster line target.
think: My **lead pay** and Jonas's teaching income cover the mortgage in this quiet picture.
Four months of **savings** provide room, though I still watch the children's costs.
do: **Keep** running the yoghurt filler and checking first sealed pots after changeovers.
**Add** fresh full-month wages to the repair fund after household bills.
feel: **Calm** about paid work while keeping an eye on ordinary family costs.
S0.quote: A neat shift report cannot seal a leaking yoghurt pot.
fieldNote: Her **daily AI use** is an existing log-search habit, checked against the physical sealer.
The **new repair saving** comes from future full pay, while the four-month reserve remains available for a wage gap.

steps.text: Keep running yoghurt filler and checking first sealed pots
Add fresh wages from full paid months to repair fund after bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the plant that software may plan milk orders and shift sheets before robots can clear a sticky filler. Our union rep should see a written paid-hours plan before a camera changes the crew size.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can learn a new control, but one lead might end up watching two lines and lose the changeover hours that help pay our mortgage. Jonas's school wage is steady; it would not replace all my pay. Four months saved buys time, not a new job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the union rep to take the proposed staffing numbers to next month's meeting. If the plant gives paid time and a quality lead, I would practise a new AI lid-defect checker on old rejected pots, never on a live batch first. I would take its guarded filler-controls course if a funded paid supervised place is offered; if no place comes, I would apply only to posted nearby lead jobs with pay and shifts that cover our bills and school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about my own hours, and interested in the checker all the same. I want the pay line in writing before I call this progress.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you put in the checker test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use a tray with a wrinkled lid, a fruit smear and one clean pot, then open each after the quality lead reviews the label. A false pass could put leaking yoghurt in a child's lunch bag.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a lower paid lead post?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if our full household budget still works without counting overtime, and the shift lets one of us collect the children. Some plants are nearby, but a job title does not tell me its wage or hours.

say: I would press for a **written hours plan** before cameras change dairy staffing.
I would ask the union to protect **paid training** when the new filler controls arrive.
think: A **two-line roster** could cut my paid changeover hours.
Jonas's **teaching wage** and our savings help, but cannot replace my whole income.
do: **Raise** written dairy staffing numbers with the union rep next month.
**Practise** new AI lid checks on old pots only with paid time and quality review.
**Take** funded guarded controls training if offered; otherwise apply for bill-covering posted lead work.
feel: **Anxious** about a plausible cut to my own hours despite interest in the test.
S1.quote: A false pass could put leaking yoghurt in a child's lunch bag.
fieldNote: She will test a **new AI checker** on old rejects with paid time and a quality lead, beyond her existing log search.
An offered **controls place** needs funding, pay and guarding; without it she limits applications to real compatible lead posts.

steps.text: Bring proposed dairy staffing numbers to union meeting
Practise new AI lid checker on old pots with paid quality review
Take guarded filler course if funded paid supervised place offered
Apply to posted nearby lead jobs if no course, pay and pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew that AGI can plan milk orders by 2028, but capable robots will not clear and seal the physical line until around 2031. We need dates for paid posts before the factory buys a whole new line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Once robots can handle the filler, I expect our five-person crew to shrink hard, perhaps including my lead shift. Jonas could still teach, but one wage and four months saved will not carry the mortgage indefinitely. I would be awake counting which payment comes after the school meals.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month we would cancel the summer cottage booking before paying its balance and add a fixed amount from each newly paid full shift to our cash reserve. I would bring our last rosters to the union's meeting on written notice and wage support. If my line hours fall, I would apply to posted local food-plant jobs only where safe duties, regular pay and school-compatible shifts cover our household bills; I would keep any paid dairy shifts until a real offer arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed by the likely loss of most of my wage. I can make calls, but I cannot make a four-month reserve last for years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the union to put in writing?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the date each dairy shift might end, the rate of any remaining job and paid notice before a cut. A list of future training courses without wages does not pay our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the reserve to retrain immediately?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not before we know whether there is an offered paid course and a posted job after it. I would keep the cash for bills while applying to actual openings, because Jonas's school salary alone is not enough.

say: I would separate **2028 planning AGI** from physical dairy robots around 2031.
I would ask the plant and union for **written shift dates** and wage support.
think: I expect our **filler crew** to lose many paid hours around 2031.
Four months saved and one **teaching wage** cannot carry the mortgage for long.
do: **Cancel** the cottage balance and save fresh full-shift pay after bills.
**Bring** rosters to the union for written notice and wage support.
**Apply** after cuts only for posted safe local food-plant work at bill-covering pay and school-compatible hours.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected major wage loss and sleepless mortgage calculations.
S2.quote: I can make calls, but I cannot make a four-month reserve last for years.
fieldNote: Her **2031 risk** is physical robot handling on the filler; planning software reaches desk tasks in 2028.
She makes **immediate cash changes**, seeks union notice and keeps current pay until a safe posted job meets family terms.

steps.text: Cancel remaining summer cottage payment this month
Save fresh wages from full dairy shifts in cash reserve
Bring rosters to union meeting for written notice and wage support
Apply after cuts to posted safe local food jobs if pay and school hours fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell colleagues that AGI may schedule dairy production in 2031, while capable robots can run the physical filler around 2034. Five years is enough to earn a real maintenance skill if the plant pays for practice, not just a video login.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 51 when robots reach the filling line. My diploma and years of faults give me a start, yet a maintenance title matters only if there is a paid opening. Jonas and I could build more than four months of savings if the full shifts continue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would put new money from each full paid quarter into our mortgage buffer. I would ask for and take a recognised filler-maintenance certificate only if the plant funds fees, gives paid release and offers supervised practice on an isolated machine. After passing, if filling hours fall, I would apply for a posted local maintenance role only if safe duties, base pay and shifts cover our bills and pickup; without the course, I would search posted food-plant lead work on those same terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, though I have time to see whether the certificate leads anywhere. I will not swap a real wage for a course brochure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What must the practical assessment test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would isolate the filler, change a worn seal and restart on a test batch with a qualified trainer beside me. I would not reach into a moving machine because a course sheet says I passed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the maintenance post worth taking?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The posting has to give a base rate and shift start, not just a possible overtime total. If the shift loses our school pickup or the rate cuts the mortgage money, I would keep earning on the filler while looking.

say: I would ask for **paid practical training** before robots reach the filler around 2034.
A **maintenance vacancy** needs posted wages, not a course promise.
think: My **lead experience** may help me qualify, but it does not guarantee a maintenance post.
Full paid shifts could grow our **mortgage buffer** before physical robots arrive.
do: **Save** new money from full paid quarters while household bills are met.
**Take** funded recognised maintenance training only with paid release and isolated supervised practice.
**Apply** for posted safe local maintenance after qualification if hours fall, or suitable lead work without a course.
feel: **Anxious** about later filler hours, with time to test a paid route.
S3.quote: I will not swap a real wage for a course brochure.
fieldNote: A **recognised certificate** requires funded fees, paid release and safe hands-on practice on an isolated filler.
Both **job searches** depend on actual safe local postings, bill-covering base pay and a shift compatible with school pickup.

steps.text: Save fresh full-quarter wages in mortgage buffer after bills
Take recognised filler course only with funded fees paid release and isolated practice
Apply for posted safe maintenance if qualified and cut, base pay and pickup fit
Search posted safe food-lead jobs if no course, base pay and pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the union that AGI could plan dairy output in 2036, while capable robots might work the filler around 2039. A decade is time to bargain for paid training places while there are still full rosters to protect.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 56 when capable robots reach the physical line. Our children may be grown, but I cannot assume the mortgage is gone or that Jonas's school wage will stay the same. Today our two wages and four-month reserve are sound; the later job count stays uncertain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading the filler and pay an extra amount off the mortgage from each actually paid overtime month after bills. I would attend the union's quarterly training committee and ask for a funded, paid, supervised controls qualification; I would enroll only when a place with isolated-machine practice is offered. After qualifying, if the filler roster shrinks, I would apply to posted safe local controls jobs only if regular pay and shift times cover our remaining bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the end of the decade, while our near-term pay feels sound. I can check a course and a vacancy before asking the family to move anything around.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave the dairy before the course ends?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, the existing filler wage pays our mortgage today. A training place is not a controls job, and I would need a written offer before giving up my shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the committee ask the plant to publish?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would ask for paid release hours, the number of real controls seats and the base rate of each posted job. One training seat for five operators would not be a fair plan.

say: I would ask the union for **real paid seats** while dairy shifts remain full.
The **2039 robot date** does not move planning AGI later than 2036.
think: At **56**, I may still need my wage for the mortgage.
Current **two-wage security** gives time, though later controls jobs are uncertain.
do: **Pay** extra mortgage principal from actually paid overtime after bills.
**Attend** quarterly union training meetings and enroll only in funded paid supervised controls practice.
**Apply** for posted safe local controls after qualification if roster shrinks and pay fits.
feel: **Uneasy** about distant job numbers while present household income remains sound.
S4.quote: A training place is not a controls job, and I would need a written offer before giving up my shift.
fieldNote: She uses the **long runway** to negotiate genuine paid course seats and job rates before ending her existing shift.
Extra **mortgage payments** use newly earned overtime; a controls application needs qualification, real cuts and suitable posted pay.

steps.text: Pay extra mortgage principal from paid overtime after bills
Attend quarterly union training committee on paid seats and jobs
Enroll in controls qualification only if funded paid isolated supervised place offered
Apply for posted safe local controls if qualified and cut, regular pay and shifts fit

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because capable robots around 2031 could remove most of our yoghurt line shifts before the mortgage is smaller. Written paid-hour notice, a real funded practical place and posted safe local work at a wage that covers our bills would help. I would want the union in the room before the plant sets the terms.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask who cleans the filler after a robot stops it at night. A sealed yoghurt pot starts with someone washing yesterday's fruit out of the machine. The line can move faster only if that person has paid time to do it safely.

headlineQuote: A sealed yoghurt pot starts with someone washing yesterday's fruit out of the machine.
portrait: **Hana**, 43, leads a yoghurt filling crew and uses her two-year technical diploma to solve sealer faults on the line.
She and **teacher partner** Jonas support two school-age children and a mortgage on typical lead pay with four months saved.
Her **daily AI use** is practical and checked against real pots; she supports union bargaining for paid time and training.
Fast **2031 robots** alarm her about losing most filler shifts, while longer warnings permit funded maintenance study and conditional job searches.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could bring capable filler robots around 2031 before her household can replace lost dairy wages.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written paid-hour notice**, funded supervised training and posted safe local work at a bill-covering wage.
